challenges.name: named-arguments-nullable-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: named arguments, defaults and nullable types
challenges.description: Call a function with a named argument, then pick the rules for nullable types, named arguments and void.

questions.explanation: Named arguments (PHP 8.0) pass a value by parameter name, so gift: true goes to $gift and $qty, which was skipped, keeps its default of 1. The result is "1 x Số đỏ (gift)". Skipping optional parameters is exactly what named arguments are for, so there is no error. Positionally, label('Số đỏ', true) would be a TypeError under strict_types (true is not an int), and in coercive mode it would quietly pass 1 as $qty.

questions.question: Which statements are true in PHP 8.4? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: A parameter like int $x = null used to become nullable implicitly; PHP 8.4 deprecates that, and the fix is to say it: ?int $x = null (or int|null $x = null). ?int is exactly the union type int|null. A positional argument after a named one is a compile error ("Cannot use positional argument after named argument"): named arguments come last. An unknown name is an Error at run time: "Unknown named parameter $quantity", which is why renaming a parameter is a breaking change once callers use names. A void function returns no value at all: return null; is a compile error, return; is the way to leave early.

options.text: function f(int $x = null) is deprecated; write ?int $x = null
label('Số đỏ', quantity: 2) throws an Error: Unknown named parameter $quantity
A function declared : void may end with return null;

challenges.name: shipping-fee-function
challenges.title: Write the delivery fee function with named parameters
challenges.description: Write shippingFee for Hồ Gươm Books: a fee by zone, a surcharge for every started 500 g above 1 kg, express at 1.5 times the delivery part, free standard delivery when a campaign threshold is reached, and insurance and cash-on-delivery surcharges that are always charged. $freeFrom is nullable: null means no campaign, 0 means free delivery for everyone. The test runner calls your function with named arguments from JSON, so missing keys use your defaults.

tests.name: Standard delivery in Hà Nội with the defaults
Insured parcel to Hồ Chí Minh City, no campaign
Campaign reached: no delivery part, the COD surcharge stays
freeFrom 0 is a campaign for every order
Express never ships free, surcharges are not multiplied
Exactly 1,500 g and exactly the campaign threshold minus one
